survey: Cartoon coconut palm on a sand dune. The trunk is a tapered, ring-segmented column. It leans slightly to the left and is sunk into the sand at its base, so it stands rather than floats; a sand mound surrounds the foot. At the top the trunk ends in a crown, and about eight broad, notched fronds spread out from it in all directions, some toward the camera and some behind. Two round coconuts hang in a cluster just under the fronds at the top of the trunk, where real palms carry their fruit. The fronds' shadow falls on the sand to the right, which fits a tree standing on the ground. A few pebbles lie half-buried in the sand. Everything joins where it should: the trunk meets the ground and the crown, the fronds come from the crown, and the coconuts hang from the crown.
